facts.statement: The genus is based on a single fossil specimen, a right premaxilla from the tip of the snout.
facts.quote: It is based on PIN 2399/301, a right premaxilla, one of the bones of the tip of the snout.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the lower Santonian-age Upper Cretaceous Yalovach Svita in the Fergana Basin of Tajikistan.
facts.quote: This specimen was found in rocks of the lower Santonian-age Upper Cretaceous Yalovach Svita of Kansai, in the Fergana Basin of Tajikistan.

facts.statement: Additional fossils assigned to the genus include vertebrae and bony armor.
facts.quote: Additional fossils including vertebrae and bony armor have been assigned to this genus.

facts.statement: The animal was estimated to be between 5 and 7 meters long.
facts.quote: It would have been a large animal, estimated at between 5 - 7 m long.

facts.statement: Kansajsuchus was described in 1975 by Mikhail Efimov.
facts.quote: Kansajsuchus was described in 1975 by Mikhail Efimov.

facts.statement: A 2019 study by Kuzmin et al. confirmed that Kansajsuchus belongs to the family Paralligatoridae.
facts.quote: However, a subsequent paper by Kuzmin et al. (2019) showed that Kansajsuchus is a member of the family Paralligatoridae.

facts.statement: The animal lived from the Cenomanian to the Campanian stages, between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Campanian (100.5 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus is classified within the family Goniopholididae.
Kansajsuchus is an extinct genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.
facts.quote: Kansajsuchus es un género extinto de mesoeucrocodilio goniofolídido.

rejected.statement: Kansajsuchus is an extinct genus of paralligatorid mesoeucrocodylian.
rejected.quote: Kansajsuchus is an extinct genus of paralligatorid mesoeucrocodylian.

rejected.statement: Researchers suggested in 2013 that future analyses might lead to abandoning the name Kansajsuchus and moving its type species to Sunosuchus.
rejected.quote: Therefore, the authors raised the suggestion that later revisions and phylogenetic analyses would result in the abandonment of the name Kansajsuchus, and a referral of its type species to Sunosuchus.
